exposure: Prenatal care with less than three visits
Infants of mothers with lower education levels
Birth weight strata: extremely low (<1000 g), very low (1000-1499 g), low (1500-2499 g), insufficient (2500-2999 g), adequate (3000-3900 g), and macrosomia (>4000 g)
finding: Low birth weight was associated with a higher risk of infant mortality, especially in infants born to younger mothers and those born in public hospitals.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was protective against infant mortality in extremely and very low birth weight infants but was a risk factor for infant mortality in infants with adequate birth weight.
